RagShortTexts: Saladin's Cairo Citadel atop the Muqattam hills anchored Mamluk military and administrative.

Variants.Content: Cairo sits at the apex of the Nile Delta and was the metropolis of the Mamluk sultanate. Saladin built the citadel on the Muqattam cliffs, and the complex held deep wells, armouries, and barracks for the royal Bahri Mamluks. Its height gave a clear view over the Al-Azhar madrasa, one of the great centres of Islamic learning. The citadel also controlled the grain supply that fed the city, and the granaries of the Nile valley reached it by river. A garrison that held the citadel could dominate Cairo and the whole of Egypt, and the sultans knew it well.

The citadel was the place where sultans were enthroned and deposed. The emir who held the garrison keys and controlled the treasury payroll had a voice in choosing the next ruler of Egypt and Syria. Officers of the royal household watched one another closely, and the wrong alliance could cost an emir his command and his life.
When the annual Nile inundation enriches the silt, barley grows taller than a man. We row heavy barges downriver to unload royal granaries beneath the fortress towers.
